name: character-invalid-non-printing-appears
description: The HED string contains a UTF-8 character.
common_causes: Copy-pasting text from documents with invisible control characters
Including non-printable characters like backspace (\b), tab, newline in tag values
Control characters with codes <= 31 or 127-159
Using curly braces {} within tag names or values (not column references)
Character encoding issues when importing from other tools
explanation: HED has strict character restrictions that are part of its specification. The name classes in the HED schemas encapsulate these restrictions.
correction_strategy: Remove or replace forbidden characters with allowed alternatives

correction_examples.explanation: Removed curly braces (only allowed in sidecars)

Label has the name class property so it can only contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. Use the Parameter-value tag instead of Label if you have values with other characters. Parameter-value has text name class which has the fewest restrictions on values.

correction_patterns: Remove control characters (codes <= 31 or 127-159)
Replace square brackets [] with parentheses () or remove
Replace tildes ~ with commas for grouping
Remove double quotes or replace with single quotes in descriptions
Remove curly braces {} unless in sidecar column references
Replace tags with restrictive name classes such as Label with less restrictive tags such as Parameter-value when necessary
fix_instructions: 1. Scan the HED string for forbidden characters
2. Identify the type of forbidden character
3. Remove or replace with appropriate alternatives
4. For control characters: simply remove them
5. For brackets/braces: use appropriate HED syntax instead
validation_hints: Check for invisible characters by examining string length vs visible content
Verify UTF-8 encoding compliance (HED 8.3.0+)
Ensure no square brackets, tildes, or double quotes remain
Confirm curly braces only appear in sidecar column references

passes: Description/This is a ʰ good character

name: curly-braces-not-in-sidecar
description: The curly brace notation is used outside a sidecar.
common_causes: Using curly braces {} in HED strings outside of sidecar column references
Mistaking column reference syntax for general HED grouping syntax
Copy-pasting sidecar HED content directly into event HED strings
explanation: Curly braces {} are reserved syntax for column references in sidecars only. They cannot be used in direct HED strings or event annotations.
correction_strategy: Remove curly braces or replace with appropriate HED grouping syntax

correction_examples.explanation: Removed invalid curly brace column reference from direct HED string
Replace curly brace placeholder with actual tag value

correction_patterns: Remove {column_name} references from direct HED strings
Use parentheses () for grouping instead of curly braces
Replace placeholder syntax with actual tag values
fix_instructions: 1. Identify curly brace usage in HED strings
2. Determine if it's intended as a column reference or grouping
3. For column references: move to sidecar or replace with actual values
4. For grouping: use parentheses instead
5. Remove any remaining curly braces
validation_hints: Curly braces are only valid in sidecar HED column definitions
Use parentheses for grouping tags together
Column references must reference actual sidecar columns

name: invalid-character-name-value-class
description: An invalid character was used in an 8.3.0 or greater style name value class.
common_causes: Using special characters (*$%[]) in tags with restrictive name classes
Including spaces in label values without using Parameter-value
Using symbols not allowed by specific tag name class restrictions
Attempting to use characters valid in text class with more restrictive classes
explanation: Different HED tags have different name class restrictions. Label tags can only contain letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores, while Parameter-value has fewer restrictions.
correction_strategy: Replace restricted tags with less restrictive ones or fix the character usage

correction_examples.explanation: Use Parameter-value for values with special characters
Replace invalid character with descriptive text
Replace spaces with hyphens in Label values

correction_patterns: Replace Label with Parameter-value for values containing special characters
Use hyphens instead of spaces in restrictive name classes
Remove or replace invalid characters (*$%[]) with valid alternatives
fix_instructions: 1. Identify the tag with invalid characters
2. Check the tag's name class restrictions
3. Either replace invalid characters or use a less restrictive tag
4. For Label: use only letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores
5. For complex values: consider using Parameter-value instead
validation_hints: Label tags have strict character restrictions
Parameter-value allows most characters including spaces and symbols
Check HED schema for specific tag name class properties

name: invalid-character-name-value-class-early-schema
description: An invalid character was as a value in a placeholder or as a tag extension.
common_causes: Using special characters in older HED schema versions with stricter character restrictions
Including characters not supported in early HED 8.x versions
Using modern character sets with legacy schema versions
explanation: Earlier HED schema versions (before 8.3.0) had more restrictive character sets and didn't support some modern characters.
correction_strategy: Upgrade to newer schema version or use only characters supported in the target schema version

correction_examples.explanation: Either upgrade schema or use text description instead of symbol
Replace special character with descriptive text

correction_patterns: Upgrade to HED schema version 8.3.0 or later for better character support
Replace special characters with descriptive text alternatives
Use basic ASCII characters for maximum compatibility
fix_instructions: 1. Check the HED schema version being used
2. Identify characters not supported in that version
3. Either upgrade to a newer schema version or replace unsupported characters
4. Use descriptive text instead of symbols when possible
5. Test with the target schema version
validation_hints: Early HED versions had stricter character restrictions
Consider upgrading to HED 8.3.0+ for better character support
Use only basic ASCII characters for maximum compatibility

name: character-invalid-structural-in-text-value
description: From HED 8.5.0 a textClass value may not contain a parenthesis, the number sign, or the tilde, the characters that change the structure of the HED string the value is substituted into.
common_causes: A parenthetical remark in a Description or other free-text value
Using # as a number sign in a value
Copying a template with its # into a value cell
Assuming a text value may contain any printable character
explanation: The value substituted for a textClass placeholder becomes part of a HED string. From HED 8.5.0 the textClass character set is value-text, which excludes the parentheses that group tags, the # that marks a placeholder, and the tilde, in addition to the comma, square brackets, and curly braces excluded before. Under earlier schemas these characters are allowed by the value class, but the substituted string is still parsed as HED, so tools report the structural error instead.
correction_strategy: Rephrase the value without the structural character

correction_examples.correct: Description/Face shown on the left side
correction_examples.explanation: The parentheses would group tags in the HED string
The # is the placeholder character of HED annotations
The tilde is a reserved character in HED strings

correction_patterns: Rephrase a parenthetical remark so the value needs no parentheses
Spell out a number as a word or drop the # before it
Use a hyphen where a tilde was meant as a connector
Single quotes, semicolons, percent signs, and non-ASCII characters remain allowed
fix_instructions: 1. Find the # placeholder that the value is substituted into and confirm it is textClass
2. Look for (, ), #, or ~ in the value
3. Rephrase the value without them
4. Check the other values of the same column
validation_hints: Only standard schema 8.5.0 and later, and libraries partnered with them, reject these characters at the value-class level
A validator that parses the substituted string first may report PARENTHESES_MISMATCH or PLACEHOLDER_INVALID instead
The comma, square brackets, and curly braces were already excluded from text values

name: character-invalid-double-quote
description: A HED string contains a double quote, which no HED string may contain whatever the value class.
common_causes: Quoting a word or a title inside a Description value
Pasting text that uses straight double quotes
Assuming a text value may contain any printable character
explanation: The double quote is one of the characters no HED string may contain anywhere (Appendix B CHARACTER_INVALID a), together with square brackets, the tilde, and the control characters. It is excluded before any value class applies, so a Description value is rejected under every schema version even though textClass allows most punctuation. A single quote (apostrophe) is allowed.
correction_strategy: Remove the double quotes or replace them with single quotes

correction_examples.explanation: Single quotes are allowed in a text value
A nameClass value allows letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, and non-ASCII characters only

correction_patterns: Replace straight double quotes with single quotes in free-text values
Remove the quote from a name or label value
fix_instructions: 1. Find the double quote the message points at
2. Remove it or replace it with a single quote
3. Check the other values of the same column for the same quoting
validation_hints: The double quote is in hed_string.forbidden of the specification's character_sets.json, so a validator reports it at the string level before the value class check
The check applies under every schema version, not only 8.3.0 and later

name: character-invalid-nonascii-boundary
description: The nonascii character set starts at code 160 (U+00A0): the C1 control characters 128-159 are forbidden everywhere, and 160 and above are allowed wherever nonascii is.
common_causes: Text copied from a Windows-1252 document, whose bytes 128-159 become C1 control characters when decoded as Latin-1
A validator that treats every character above 127 as non-ASCII and so admits the C1 controls
A validator that starts nonascii at 128 or rejects characters by a printable test instead of the code ranges
explanation: The specification's nonascii set is utf-8 codes 160 and above, and no HED string may contain the control characters 0-31 or 127-159 (Appendix B CHARACTER_INVALID a). The two ranges meet at U+009F and U+00A0: U+009F is a C1 control and is invalid in every value, while U+00A0 (no-break space) is the first nonascii character and is valid wherever nonascii is, including a nameClass value under standard schema 8.5.0, whose nameClass declaration lists nonascii.
correction_strategy: Replace the control character with the intended character, or remove it

correction_examples.explanation: U+009F is a C1 control, usually a decoding artifact; the intended character is a letter

correction_patterns: Re-decode text that came from a Windows-1252 source so its bytes 128-159 become the intended characters
Remove C1 control characters from values
fix_instructions: 1. Find the character the message points at and its code point
2. If it is in 128-159, it is a C1 control: replace it with the intended character or remove it
3. A character at 160 or above is allowed wherever the value class allows nonascii; no change is needed
validation_hints: Use the code ranges of hed_string.forbidden in character_sets.json, not a printable test: U+00A0 is not printable in some runtimes but is a valid nonascii character
The nonascii regex of character_sets.json is [^\x00-\x9F], so 128-159 are excluded by the set as well as by the forbidden ranges
Under 8.5.0 the nameClass declaration lists nonascii; under 8.3.0 and 8.4.0 validators apply nonascii from the specification's defaults

name: character-invalid-text-value-before-8-5-0
description: Under standard schemas before 8.5.0 a textClass value uses the text character set: printable or non-ASCII characters except comma, square brackets, and curly braces, with the double quote and tilde excluded from every HED string.
common_causes: A square bracket or double quote in a Description value
Applying the 8.5.0 value-text restrictions to a dataset annotated with an earlier schema
Applying the character list the 8.0.0 to 8.2.0 schemas declare for textClass, which omits the underscore and the apostrophe
explanation: Before standard schema 8.5.0 a textClass value may contain any printable or non-ASCII character except the comma, square brackets, and curly braces (the text set of section 2.2), and the double quote and tilde that no HED string may contain; before 8.3.0 the non-ASCII characters are excluded from every HED string as well. Both validators have always applied the text set there, also under 8.0.0 to 8.2.0, whose schemas declare an explicit list without the underscore and the apostrophe; the specification's character_sets.json records text as the default for those versions, so file names and contractions remain valid. From 8.5.0 the value-text set also excludes parentheses, the number sign, and the tilde.
correction_strategy: Remove the square bracket, curly brace, or double quote from the value, or rephrase

correction_examples.explanation: Square brackets are excluded from every HED string
Already valid: the underscore is allowed in a text value under every schema version

correction_patterns: Rephrase a bracketed remark without the brackets
Keep underscores, apostrophes, percent signs, and semicolons: they are valid text characters
fix_instructions: 1. Find the placeholder the value is substituted into and confirm it is textClass
2. Look for [, ], {, }, or a double quote in the value
3. Remove or rephrase
4. Do not change underscores or apostrophes; they are allowed
validation_hints: The text set is the value_class_defaults.textClass entry of character_sets.json for standard versions before 8.5.0
The 8.0.0 to 8.2.0 schemas declare an explicit character list for textClass; validators apply text instead, as the specification records
Parentheses, the number sign, and the tilde are structural characters: a validator may report PARENTHESES_MISMATCH or PLACEHOLDER_INVALID for them, and from 8.5.0 value-text excludes them
